An indoor X-band tracking radar system was developed to measure dynamic RCS of mini-UAVs in flight.
The UAV used was a Parrot™ AR.Drone quadcopter, 0.51 m long and 0.45 m wide.
Radar frequency range used was 8–10 GHz with a peak output power of 35.5 dBm.
The radar used a 55 ms coherent pulse interval with 288 Hz pulse repetition frequency.
UAV position and orientation were tracked using 24 ceiling-mounted infrared cameras with 1 cm and 1° accuracy.
Dynamic RCS measurements showed significantly higher values than static RCS measurements.
Static RCS measurements often showed deep nulls at specific aspect angles, which dynamic measurements averaged out.
Dynamic RCS modeling used lognormal PDFs fitted to 10° yaw aspect bins.
The 50% probability of detection range increased by 15% when using dynamic RCS models compared to static ones.
The UAV's propellers rotate fully every 2 ms, contributing to dynamic RCS fluctuations.
Radar calibration included I/Q channel gain adjustment and boresight calibration using a 6-inch calibration sphere.
Left censoring in RCS measurements was handled by incorporating censored data likelihood in statistical modeling.
The decorrelation angle for the AR.Drone at 9 GHz was estimated as 0.0245 radians (1.4°).
The radar antenna had a beamwidth of 7° elevation and 12° azimuth.
Probability of detection was computed using the Marcum Q function integrating over the RCS PDFs.
The dynamic RCS measurement system can only measure UAVs with RCS greater than approximately −34.8 dBsm due to marker size and materials.
The UAV was equipped with three 11 mm diameter spherical motion capture markers for tracking.
The radar system used a quasi-monostatic antenna arrangement with two X-band standard gain horn antennas.
The indoor radar range was 7.2 m swath length with azimuth scanning from −95° to +95° and elevation from −45° to +45°.
The study showed that radar frequency selection affects detection range, with 8 GHz optimal for single-pulse detection and 8.5 GHz for cumulative detection over multiple pulses.
